Definition: from G583; an enrollment; by implication, an assessment:--taxing.
BiblicalUsage: Twice, and both times about a taxing. Luke dates the birth of Christ by the first taxing, when Cyrenius was governor of Syria, in Luke 2:2, and Gamaliel remembers Judas of Galilee, who rose up in the days of the taxing in Acts 5:37 and drew away much people after him.
TheologicalSignificance: The word is a census and a tax roll — Rome counting its subjects — and Luke uses it to date the birth of the King Rome never counted on.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
